text:
kevin: Heads-up, bringing up Nimbus-9B for onboarding. Quick tokenizer smoke showed a weird high-id sentinel 57888 that decodes to a private glyph (). vendor export log mentions a "placeholder_token" insertion. Anyone seen a 57k+ sentinel before? :thinking:

maya: can you paste a tiny encode/decode example and the reported ckpt_vocab_size? helps decide whether it's appended or inside table.

kevin: REPL: 
```
>>> tok.encode("Quick \u00ADsplit test")
[412, 57888, 71, 2]
>>> tok.decode([412,57888,71,2])
"Quick \uF222split test"
```
checkpoint reports vocab_size=49512 so sentinel > vocab_size (appended). Also vendor config: rotary_base: 9000, rotary_per_layer_scale: [1.0,0.98,1.03,...] length == n_layers.

ron: two things to watch: 1) appended sentinel means IDs after it in vendor tooling might have been shifted during export; 2) rotary_base=9000 + per-layer scales is nonstandard for us (we expect 8192, single per-head/group scaling). Both can produce subtle regressions.

ida: I ran a quick AWQ-int4 conversion (default) on the raw checkpoint: summarization ROUGE-L -2.5% vs fp16, long-dialog BLEU -0.9, MMLU -0.2. So main hit on long-form generation.

eval-bot: staging run: {"model":"nimbus9b-awq-int4","rouge_l":"-2.5%","bleu":"-0.9","mmlu":"-0.2","tokens":"105k"}

maya: for the sentinel my bias is minimal invasive: add an id_alias mapping 57888 -> PAD (0) applied during tokenization, and if 57888 < ckpt_vocab_size then do a sparse copy emb[0] = emb[57888] during conversion. That avoids reordering the whole embedding matrix. Also persist id_alias.json in the converted artifact.

kevin: agreed. I'll add id_alias.json and conversion metadata (src_vocab_size, dst_vocab_size, aliases_applied). Also wire a small unit test to assert max(token_id) < vocab_size after conversion.

ron: on rotary: since vendor has rotary_base=9000 and per-layer scales, we should normalize to our runtime by combining base rescale and per-layer compensation. Pseudocode: 
```python
base_scale = 8192.0 / float(model.config.get('rotary_base', 8192))
for layer_idx in range(n_layers):
    scale = base_scale / float(model.config.get('rotary_per_layer_scale', [1.0]*n_layers)[layer_idx])
    model.layers[layer_idx].rotary.inv_freq *= scale
# recompute sin/cos caches if precomputed
```
I ran a small headwise cosine similarity check vs fp16 after normalization: max diff < 3e-4 on a 8-token sample.

ida: nice. I'll string alias + sparse-copy + rotary-normalize into a conversion hook and re-run AWQ/GPTQ pipeline tonight with a targeted long-summary slice to catch the ROUGE regression.

maya: two extra test suggestions: 1) kv-cache alignment probe: feed a short prompt and check that cached key/value shapes and lookup indices align between fp16 and converted model for the same token stream. 2) a tokenization roundtrip test for soft-hyphen (U+00AD) cases since our REPL showed split around it. For the soft-hyphen we should canonicalize by stripping U+00AD during canonical pre-tokenize normalization (NFC + drop U+00AD) so token ids match our standard tokenizers.

kevin: good catch on soft-hyphen. I'll add normalization step to conversion: unicode.normalize('NFC') then replace U+00AD with '' unless model config sets keep_soft_hyphen flag. Also will persist token_normalization.json documenting the change.

build-bot: CI scheduled: nimbus9b conversion + eval (awq, gptq, full eval battery) on staging-pool at 03:00 UTC, est duration 7h. branch: feat/nimbus-sentinel-rotary-normalize.

ida: after conversion + normalization, if AWQ still shows ROUGE drop we should try a small fine-tune/quant-finetune on summarization prompts (1-2k steps) and see if that recovers quality cheaply. but only if conversion-normalize doesn't fix it.

ron: one more operational note: retain original rotary_per_layer_scale in rotary_metadata.json so we can audit pre/post values. Also add an opt-in runtime flag use_model_native_rotary to skip normalization if a downstream team wants vendor behavior.

maya: +1 to metadata and runtime flag. I'll add unit tests: (A) encode->alias->embed->decode roundtrip for randomized short strings including U+00AD cases, (B) kv-cache alignment check, (C) headwise cos-sim threshold check.

kevin: thanks team. I'll open PR with conversion hook & tests, run overnight evals and post diffs here tomorrow morning. :coffee:
